html:
SMTO-BOOT-0024 — The installer couldn't load the NVIDIA graphics driver

GUID: 2d8ed03b-3267-415a-8d16-a482543d5dd1
Slug: boot-cuda-driver-missing
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • To choose the right vLLM build, the installer talks directly to the NVIDIA driver, the software that runs your graphics card. It couldn't load the driver, so it stopped before installing vLLM.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Run nvidia-smi in the same terminal. If it fails or doesn't list your card, install or repair the NVIDIA driver for your graphics card. nvidia-smi and the installer both need the NVIDIA driver; if nvidia-smi fails, the driver itself is the problem.
  2. If you run the installer inside a container or WSL, make sure graphics card access is turned on for it. The installer loads the driver file libcuda.so.1, which a container or WSL only provides when graphics card access is set up.
  3. If the driver install asks for a restart, finish or stop any running work first, then restart the computer and run nvidia-smi again. A newly installed driver may not load until the computer restarts.
  4. Before running the installer again, run conda env list. If the environment name you used is listed, choose a new name or remove that half-built environment first. The driver check also runs after the environment is created, and the installer won't reuse a name that already exists.

What success looks like

  • nvidia-smi lists your graphics card, and the installer prints lines starting with "CPU:" and "GPU 0:" instead of this message.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full terminal output, including the SMTO-BOOT-0024 line, plus the output of nvidia-smi, and send it to the person who manages this computer's graphics drivers. Don't delete Conda or SMTO files to get past this; the installer couldn't reach the graphics driver.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • vllm_install_support.py could not load libcuda.so.1 through ctypes (OSError) while probing hardware for install-vllm.sh, so no GPU list or driver CUDA version was available.

What this means

  • Hardware probing attempts to load libcuda.so.1 with ctypes and catches an OS loader error. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Hardware probing attempts to load libcuda.so.1 with ctypes and catches an OS loader error.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect driver installation and authorized host/container library visibility.

How to fix it

  • Make libcuda.so.1 loadable for the Conda Python that runs the helper: install or repair the NVIDIA driver, or expose the driver libraries to the container or WSL2 instance (check ldconfig -p | grep libcuda and nvidia-smi). Earlier steps may already have installed Miniforge or created the new environment; if it exists, rerun with a new name or remove it first.
  • Restore the host NVIDIA driver and authorized GPU/container access.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The selected environment loads the intended driver library successfully.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
